applies_why: The judge is comparing two chains and treats the challenger's footed seed/loins chain as underdetermined because of what it does not explicitly name, which is the chain-vs-chain footing and word-for-word issue K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: does not name Joseph as the begetter: one reading is a forbidden demand for explicit naming or word-for-word statement; the other is a mere support gap in the chain's footing; I read the judge as using it as a defect despite calling the chain footed.
why: Because the judge treats a footed chain as weaker for not explicitly naming Joseph, it applies the explicit-statement test K-C retires in chain-vs-chain weighing.
